original_answer: The speech (audio-text) alignment quality was evaluated through a manual human evaluation. Two annotators each rated 30 items from each bin, with 10 shared items to compute inter-annotator reliability [1]. The audio-text alignment was rated on a 3-point scale: 1 (wrong alignment), 2 (partial alignment, some words or sentences may be missing), 3 (correct alignment, allowing non-spoken syllables at start or end) [1]. Ratings were binned by hunalign confidence (Low/Moderate/High) and averaged over 90 items and two raters, with an average audio-text alignment score of 0.61 out of 3 [7]. Inter-annotator reliability for audio-text alignment ratings was measured with Krippendorff's α and scored 1.00 [8], and the alignment was rated as generally high quality [9].

The inter-annotator agreement between two raters was measured by Krippendorff’s α-reliability score (Krippendorff, 2013) for ordinal ratings. The inter- annotator reliability for text-to-text alignment quality ratings scored 0.77, while for audio-text alignment quality ratings it scored 1.00.

The audio-text alignment was rated as in general as high qual- ity. The text-text alignment rating increases correspond- ing to increasing hunalign conﬁdence score which shows that the latter can be safely used to ﬁnd a threshold for corpus ﬁltering. Overall, the audio-text and text-text alignment scores are very similar to those reported by Kocabiyikoglu et al.
